bifurcation.note: Declared before any measurement. Every score below rests on counted strings, counted runs, counted (npc,race) pairs, frames and pixel fractions, not on an impression of how the scene looks. Two screenshots are cited and both are cited for something countable — the '1 of 13' progress string on the panel header, and the presence of the interlocutor as an untextured capsule. RI-JRN01 M5's opaque-area figure is a pixel readback and is treated as a number, not as an image judgement.

checks.note: 33 of 45. Measured with MY instrument, not the builder's: the accessor is __HARNESS.getRenderedText() (W1-26's draw-call register, which wraps fillText and shadows the clip) rather than getCensusState().surface.rendered_text (UILayer.metrics(), a layout echo). The two agree on this scene at every node — 0 strings claimed by metrics().text that the draw register did not see — so the a-priori objection to the builder's accessor is WITHDRAWN on the evidence. 10 of 10 question texts genuinely reach the frame. The shortfall is the denominator: the builder counts the strings buildCensusModel KEPT, which is the exact layer round 2's defect lived in, and against what the census actually computes for each node the ratio is 0.85/0.87.

checks.value: AC = 6 of 7 (threshold >= 6). Six of the six consumed answers are evidenced by lines from ONE template — the writ's identity block.
checks.note: 12 of 30. The count passes. The item's one declared judgement call is whether the seven quotes are seven templates, and it instructs the critic to score the axis at its floor if they are. Drawn evidence: 'Name recorded: Silence-Under-Salt' / 'Also called: Silence-Under-Salt' / 'Observed as: Saxhleel' / 'Raised at: black water, no bottom' / 'Trade declared: Xanmeer-Delver' / 'Tide drawn on: ...'. Every one is a field of the same printed form. The RESPONSIVE lines that would make this a conversation — the upbringing reply 'The interior. I will write the marsh...', the birthsign reply 'The tide was in and the root had more than it needed...', and the naming line itself — are computed into state.spoken and thrown away by ui.js's overflow-sacrifice loop before fillText. Three of the six survive only as form fields. The item's own How-we-lose: 'a scene that repeats every answer back is a receipt, not a conversation.' Only race carries both a drawn responsive line and a form line.

reference_items.why_not_ten: The moment the questionnaire exists for does not reach the frame. RI-CHR01 §4 calls the Warden-Scribe saying the profession aloud 'the moment the route is for'; measured at the node it is spoken, it is drawn in 0 of 12 named runs, because ui.js drops `spoken` lines from the front until the panel's 48%-of-height budget is met and the naming line is always the line that goes. The scene is legible and it is not yet an exchange: AC = 6 of 7 is carried entirely by a printed form.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Three changes. (1) The naming line must be unclippable at writ.birthsign. Either give it the same protection `line` has in ui.js's sacrifice order (it is the reply that matters most and it is sacrificed first), or hold it as the node's own `line` at a dedicated node between the last question and the birthsign, the way Morrowind gives Ergalla his own beat to say 'you are a Battlemage'. (2) Fix jrn09-exchange.mjs M3 to test the naming LINE, not the class name substring. (3) Raise DTR under the census-state denominator by drawing the scribe's framing line at every questionnaire node or removing it from the state, so that 'computed' and 'kept by the model builder' are the same set. Acceptance: NAMED_line >= 99% over >= 240 completions measured at the node the line is spoken; DTR_scene >= 0.90 against getCensusState(); AC >= 6 of 7 with at least four of the six evidenced by a drawn responsive line rather than a writ field.

checks.note: 15 of 15. The panel-budget trade did NOT break M5. Round 2's pixel max on the same method was 0.49; PANEL_MAX_FRAC 0.42 -> 0.48 moved it to 0.498, about 0.008 of frame area. But the builder's counter-check reads getCensusState().surface.opaque_area_frac = UILayer.metrics(), which amended M5 explicitly forbids ('never taken from the build's own layout report'), and it understates the readback by 0.114. It is the safe direction for a critic and it is the same instrument in both rounds, which is what makes the comparison meaningful.

reference_items.why_not_ten: Three of the four caps BAR-CRITIQUE-W1-07-R1 §R9 listed are closed this round — HF7 (0 of 14 professions -> 14 of 14), M8's new hard fail (the writ is drawn and openable), and HF9 (a title surface exists, by W1-26). HF5 is not, and §1.1 caps the item at 2 for it. Underneath the cap the item also fails M4 clause 1 by a factor of about 360 — 0.17 s of play before the first character-defining question against O6's 60 s — and scores 0 on M9/M15 because the accessor those checks were gated on cannot see the surface they are aimed at.
reference_items.path_to_ten: In this order. (1) Run M13's other two legs — mouse+keyboard and CDP touch emulation at 390x844 landscape. The census already takes only `interact`/`block`/a direction and the touch layer exists (__HARNESS.touchDown/touchLayout), so this is a probe, not a feature. HF5 lifts and the item's real number becomes visible. (2) Instrument the third surface AND make it enumerable: either route game/src/ui/glyphs.js drawText() through a fillText-shaped shim, or have UISurface.el() push {surface:'menus', text} into the same register, and add 'menus' to surfaces_instrumented. Then M9/M15 become measurable and 'Take A tithe-gourd, empty' can be judged instead of hidden. (3) O6: give the player the barge hold before Jeeh-Ei asks anything — walkable, with the tithe-gourd takeable and Jeeh-Ei present — and emit first_control when the character first accepts a movement input. Acceptance: 4/4 modality legs complete; getRenderedText().surfaces_instrumented includes 'menus' and returns >= 5 entries on a HUD frame; getJourneyStamps().available_play_s_before_first_field >= 60 on a play-mode boot.

reference_items.why_not_ten: Round 2's `coupling == 0` on greetings and race-gated topics is genuinely closed and proved by perturbation with restore — that is real work and it is the second-best consumption proof in this corpus. What replaces it is two measured failures: every one of the 300 greeting cells is exactly five lines, which the axis names as a generator's signature and scores 0; and only 53 of the 300 cells have ever been observed drawn, against a floor of 100.
reference_items.path_to_ten: (1) Distribution: give the cells authored counts. A hostile Dres factor greeting a Saxhleel should have more to say than a neutral net-mender greeting a Breton, and the axis's 10 band asks for a stated authored reason for every cell that sits at the floor of five. (2) Consumption: drive >= 250 of 300 cells in a live sweep — the 12 reaction groups x 5 bands need NPCs at every disposition band, which means moving disposition in play rather than only at spawn. (3) Make infoFor()'s generic level live: author at least one actorless info per topic so a new NPC is never mute by default, and re-run creation-audit's CHR02-nobody-is-mute over the full 52-NPC roster. Acceptance: cell-size histogram with >= 4 distinct sizes; >= 250 cells observed drawn; 0 of 520 mute pairs.

reference_items.why_not_ten: The birthsign is not a decision. Measured for the first time by a tool that landed today, every one of the nine signs is viable with all six class families and all ten races — 540 of 540 — which is this axis's own definition of nine small bonuses rather than nine choices. And the one sign built to be a real cost, the Dry Well, still costs nothing observable because nothing in the build spends Focus.
reference_items.path_to_ten: (1) Make at least one sign non-viable with at least two class families, as the axis requires of the Dry Well specifically. build-viability.mjs's four criteria (main_quest, three_factions_rank5, no_unpassable_gate, tier5_survivable) are the instrument and they currently return zero failures on all 540, so the tuning target is measurable to the row. (2) Close the Focus-spend seam with W1-14 so the Dry Well's drawback moves a number a player watches. Acceptance: build-viability reports the Dry Well non-viable with >= 2 families and >= 1 other sign non-viable with >= 1; and a live trace showing focus falling below max and failing to regenerate under the Dry Well.

checks.observed: The player's race, chosen in the creation scene, is read at 60 Hz by converse.js against requires.race / forbids.race and changes what a live NPC will say. biggest_gap.what: RI-CHR01 §4 states the questionnaire's purpose in its own words — the Warden-Scribe says the profession aloud, 'which is the moment the route is for' — and RI-JRN09 M3 requires that line on the frame in 100% of named runs. Measured at the node the line is spoken (writ.birthsign, its only opportunity, because `spoken` carries only the reply to the last answer): 0 of 12 named runs across six races and two upbringings. The mechanism is ui.js's overflow-sacrifice loop — `while (contentH > maxH && spokenLines.length) spokenLines.shift()` — which drops the scribe's previous reply from the front until the panel fits its 48%-of-frame-height budget, and at the birthsign node (nine options plus a two-line naming sentence) the naming line is always what goes. The builder's own instrument reports 100% because it does not test that line: jrn09-exchange.mjs M3 runs `blob.indexOf(norm(c.class_name)) >= 0` over the concatenated drawn text of every node in the walk, and the same round added 'Trade declared: %ClassName' to the writ's drawn identity block at writ.stamp, so the class name is on the frame whatever the scribe did or did not say. Measured side by side on the same twelve runs: the naming LINE 0 of 12; the class NAME substring 12 of 12. The same mechanism eats the upbringing reply ('The interior. I will write the marsh. There are people here who will read that and stand up straighter, and people who will read it and count their doors.') and the birthsign reply ('The tide was in and the root had more than it needed. It gave you a swallow it did not owe you.'), which is why AC = 6 of 7 is evidenced entirely by fields of one printed form.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: Morrowind's opening is remembered because a bored functionary looks at your answers and tells you what you apparently are. This build computes that sentence, writes it, carries it through the model, exposes it through the harness — and clips it off the bottom of the panel, then prints the word on a form two nodes later. A player answers ten questions about wounded dogs and toll-houses and is never told anything; they later find a noun on a document. Round 3 closed round 2's orphan-text defect on the questions and opened the same defect on the answer, and the round's own instrument certified it closed. That is the third time in this project a measurement has passed because it tested something adjacent to what the item asked for, and it is the exact failure BAR-CRITIQUE-W1-07-R1 filed RI-JRN09 to prevent.

remedy.action: Two changes and a test, in this order. (1) Give the naming moment its own beat. The line is the payoff of a ten-node route and it is currently one entry in a `spoken` array that the layout treats as the least important thing on the panel. Add a node between the last question and writ.birthsign whose `line` IS the naming sentence and whose only input is an acknowledgement — the same shape writ.stamp was given this round for exactly this reason — so it occupies the one slot ui.js never sacrifices. Morrowind gives Socucius Ergalla his own beat to say 'you are a Battlemage'; this is that beat. (2) If the sacrifice loop is kept, make it declare what it dropped: have UILayer._redraw record the sacrificed lines in `metrics().sacrificed` so that any probe reading the surface can see the difference between 'not computed' and 'computed and thrown away'. Round 3's own defect is invisible in every instrument the build ships. (3) Fix tools/harness/jrn09-exchange.mjs M3 to test the naming LINE at the node it is spoken, not the class-name substring over the whole walk. The current test cannot go red while the writ draws the class name, which makes it a probe that cannot fail.
targets: game/data/dialogue/topics/writ-house.json (a node between writ.class-questions and writ.birthsign carrying on_match_named_class / on_nearest_named_class as its `line`)
game/src/character/census.js (case 'writ.class-named' — advance to the new node rather than straight to writ.birthsign)
tools/harness/jrn09-exchange.mjs (M3 NAMED_line: assert the line, at its node)
remedy.acceptance: Over >= 240 completions covering all 10 races x 4 upbringings with a published a/b/c/d histogram: the text of on_match_named_class / on_nearest_named_class appears in __HARNESS.getRenderedText() at the node it is spoken in >= 99% of named runs, measured by corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-07-r3/critic-w1-07-r3g.mjs unchanged. Separately, deleting the naming line from writ-house.json must take that figure to 0 and restoring it must return it — the delete-the-fix check this round applied to the greeting data and not to this. And AC's drawn evidence must include >= 4 responsive lines rather than 6 fields of the writ.

secondary_observations.what: THE SECOND-BIGGEST GAP, AND THE ONE THAT DECIDES THE MORROWIND COMPARISON: you are a form before you are a body. RI-JRN01 M4 clause 1 — O6, '>= 60 s of available play before the first character-defining question' — was corpus_debt for two rounds because journey-run.mjs and the first_control event did not exist. Both landed today, so I measured it, and it is the first time anyone has. On a play-mode boot: the title appears, `New` is pressed, and the census is already sitting on hold.hatch-name. first_field_frame is 10, i.e. 0.17 s at 60 Hz, against a threshold of 60 s. `first_control` never fires at all — first_control_frame is still null after 5,179 frames. The player is asked their hatch-name before they have ever moved. Morrowind's whole trick is the other way round: you wake, you walk the length of a ship, you meet Jiub, you climb stairs, you step onto a dock, you walk into an office — minutes of embodied play — and only then does anyone ask you anything. This is RI-JRN01's own How-we-lose #5, 'control arrives after definition', and the bar critic called O6 'the single best idea in the area'. It is not the piece's fault that nobody could measure it before today; it is the piece's gap now.

THE RENDERED-TEXT ACCESSOR IS HONEST AND INCOMPLETE, AND THE INCOMPLETENESS IS STRUCTURAL. render/text-register.js is a genuinely good instrument — fed by the draw call, clip-aware, explicitly not a second copy of the model — and it reproduced the builder's DTR numbers exactly when I pointed it at the census. But render/renderer.js owns THREE 2D text surfaces (ui, title, menus) and instruments TWO, under a comment that says 'Every 2D surface this renderer owns is registered against the one rendered-text register'. I instrumented the third at runtime through the register's own public instrument() and got ZERO entries — because game/src/ui/glyphs.js drawText() renders every glyph as a stroked Path (moveTo / lineTo / quadraticCurveTo / stroke) and never calls fillText. The register wraps fillText and strokeText. It is therefore structurally incapable of seeing W1-21's entire UI system, instrumented or not. Enumerated through UISurface.elements[].text instead, the opening draws five strings the accessor cannot see: '5', '0', 'LIGHT', 'Spark-Dart' and 'Take A tithe-gourd, empty'. M9's domain is 'every string rendered OUTSIDE a dialogue/journal/book surface' — which is exactly the surface it cannot see. W1-26's own probe records `surfaces_searched: 'title (the only non-dialogue drawn surface in the build)'`, which is false. Per RI-JRN01 §0.1(a) I score M9 and M15 unmeasurable => 0 rather than passing a grep over a set that excludes its own subject, and I note that this is the round-2 failure — a grep over an empty accessibility tree reading as a clean pass — reproduced one layer down by the fix written to close it.

THE PANEL-BUDGET TRADE DID NOT COST M5, AND THE BUILDER'S PROOF THAT IT DIDN'T IS INADMISSIBLE. Round 3 raised PANEL_MAX_FRAC 0.42 -> 0.48 and OPTION_WINDOW 5 -> 9 to buy delivery, and shipped a counter-check reading getCensusState().surface.opaque_area_frac. Amended M5 says the figure is 'measured from a readback of the frame and never taken from the build's own layout report', and that is precisely the number the counter-check reads. Measured properly with the round-2 critic's pixel detector verbatim: 0.2954-0.4980 against the 0.55 ceiling, where the build self-reports 0.1681-0.3837. M5 passes. Round 2's pixel maximum on the same detector was 0.49, so the trade cost about 0.008 of frame area — a real answer to the question, and one the builder had no admissible evidence for. What it did cost is headroom: the claimed 0.166 is actually 0.052, and the same panel budget is what throws the naming line away. Instinct says a builder that buys one bar by spending another should be caught; here the bar it spent held, and the thing it actually spent was the scribe's voice.

540 OF 540 IS SIMULTANEOUSLY A 10 AND A 0. tools/analysis/build-viability.mjs landed today and unblocked two axes that had been corpus_debt since wave 0. Its first run reports 540 of 540 signatures viable — 10 races x 9 birthsigns x 6 class families, zero failures on all four criteria. RI-CHR01's Distinctness axis wants '540 signatures, >= 486 viable' and scores that 10. RI-CHR03's Decidability axis names 'every sign viable with all 6 (nine small bonuses)' as its 0. The build sits exactly at the point where one axis is maximised and the other is zero, and the two items have been reading the same number in opposite directions for a whole wave without either being measured. Whichever way the project resolves it, one of those two bands has to move, and the resolution is a corpus question rather than a builder's.

THE MUTE-PAIR FIX WAS DATA, NOT A RULE, AND IT HELD FOR ONE DAY. My own bare-Node census confirms the builder's headline at the scope it was measured in: 0 of 150 (npc,race) pairs mute over the 15 NPCs in game/data/npcs/{named-states,writ-house,thorn}.json, per-race topic totals 56-57 across all ten races, no settlement silent for anyone, and the differentiation running in the right direction — of 57 (npc,topic) pairs exactly one is subtractive and 35 vary the answer. That is a good fix and the Saxhleel finding that motivated it was the best thing in the round. But game/data/npcs/mainline.json (37 more NPCs) landed at 227947b, after the piece's commit, and creation-audit at my HEAD now reports 370 of 520 (npc,race) pairs mute, 77 dangling (npc,topic) pairs, 15 of 52 NPCs carrying an actor row, and race-still-changes-the-answer at 23.1% against its 30% floor. The new data is not W1-07's; the architecture is. The builder itself measured that 0 of 306 topics carries an actorless info, which makes infoFor()'s third precedence level dead code, and then closed the gap by hand-authoring 33 topics for the fifteen people it knew about rather than by making the fallback work. A consumer whose default for an unknown NPC is silence will go on producing this result every time the world grows.

THE TEN ANSWERS ARE ROUNDED AWAY, AND THAT IS NEW THIS ROUND. Exact set-equality matches: 1 of 240. So in 239 of 240 runs the class is assigned by the new nearest-profession fit, and census.js then sets spec.custom = null and spec.classId = c.id — the character takes the canned class and the shape the answers derived is discarded. Measured over 233 named runs, the mean overlap between the five skills the player's answers produced and the five skills of the class actually adopted is 2.66 of 5; 95 of 233 keep two or fewer; one keeps none at all. Before round 3, named_class was null in essentially every play, so the questionnaire gave the player exactly the shape their answers derived. Closing HF7 therefore made the route name you something and stop listening to you at the same time. This is defensible — Morrowind's questionnaire also lands you in one of a fixed set of classes — and it is a real change in what the ten questions do, made to satisfy a bar, and nobody recorded it.

THE UNNAMED BAND IS ONE TUNED CONSTANT AND DOES NO OTHER WORK. RI-JRN09's How-we-lose warns that 'NAMED is met by widening the matcher until everything is named'. The build's answer is nearest_profession_floor: 4, chosen from a percentile table to leave about 4% unnamed. I swept it: at floor 0 — no floor at all — the matcher still reaches 14 of 14 distinct classes and names 100% of runs; at floor 10 it names 51.7% and reaches 13. So the floor buys the honest 'I do not have a word for what you are' band and buys nothing else. That is not a cheat — NAMED_distinct is 14 of 14 at every floor from 0 to 8, and the constant is read at runtime from creation-questions.json so it perturbs, which is good practice — but the band the item explicitly protects exists because of one number somebody picked, not because some answers genuinely resist naming.

THE INTERLOCUTORS HAVE NO FACES, AND THAT IS THE REST OF THE MORROWIND ANSWER. Both screenshots this verdict cites show the same thing: a well-lit room with real furniture — a wall of eleven years of other people's reed-cases behind the desk, beams, a hanging lamp — and, standing in it, untextured capsules. Jeeh-Ei is a beige blob with a lighter blob for a head. Tuleeh-Ma is a green blob behind the panel. Nobody has eyes, nobody moves while they speak, nobody looks at you. Morrowind's Socucius Ergalla is not a technical achievement either, but he has a face that turns, an idle, and a voice grunt, and the scene depends on the sense of being looked at by a bored official. The builder records this honestly as 'art, not wiring' and it is out of scope for a wiring round. It is in scope for the owner's question, and no bar in this corpus measures it: RI-JRN01 M6 asks only that the speaker resolve to a live NPC record, which it does, 18 of 18.

THE TREE MOVED UNDER THIS MEASUREMENT AND I AM RECORDING WHAT I SAW RATHER THAN PRETENDING IT DID NOT. The piece was committed at b3c6f43. Between my first probe and my last, bcc2567 (W1-26 — title.js, text-register.js, and the move of the '1 of 13' scroll note into the panel header) and b48859f (W1-21 — the interface) landed, and 227947b (37 new NPC records) was already in. My first DTR run recorded one clipped string at hold.hatch-name; my second, twenty minutes later, recorded zero, because W1-26 had fixed exactly that clip in between. Boot broke six times during this session on another piece's half-written quest data ('hooks.json: 23 quest(s) seed no topic from a journal write', then 'this._buildUI is not a function'), and smoke.mjs passed 6/6 before and after. Load reached 37 on four cores with 42 chrome processes, which is the condition AGENT-PROTOCOL now names as the point at which agents stop measuring and start preventing each other from measuring. Every figure in this verdict was taken at b48859f unless it says otherwise, and the figures I attribute to round 2 are quoted, not re-run.

PHANTOM TOOLS 67 -> 55, AND IT CHANGES THE ARITHMETIC OF THIS PIECE. tools/analysis/build-viability.mjs, tools/journey/{journey-run,beat-extract,gamepad-shim,state-diff}.mjs and all five of RI-EXP01's tools now exist on disk. So the corpus_debt that BAR-CRITIQUE-W1-07-R1 identified as making three of this piece's six items unpassable by construction HAS EXPIRED BY ITS OWN CONDITION, and the bar critic's honest instruction — 'do not dispatch W1-07 round 4 against the old bars' — no longer applies. Two of those newly-runnable axes I ran, and one of them (RI-CHR03 Decidability) comes back at its 0 band on its first measurement, which is the system working. RI-EXP01 is now a critic's debt rather than the corpus's, and I did not discharge it: session-run.mjs exists and I did not run it, so N_found, T_lie, T_refusal and N_odd remain unmeasured on any build for a fourth round. That is mine and it is the second thing round 4's critic should do.

The dispatch brief instructed me to score it as a hard fail because W1-07 declined to attempt it in a shared tree; that reasoning was sound as coordination and would have been wrong as measurement, and I am recording both halves.

corpus_extended.what: No method in RI-JRN01 can see either AR-2 failure this verdict records. M5 measures area, M6 measures attribution, M9 greps a fixed substring list ('Press ', 'Tap ', 'Click ', 'Tutorial', 'Objective', 'Quest added', 'New quest', 'Tip:') that contains neither ' of ' nor 'Take ', and M9's accessor cannot reach the surface both strings are drawn on. O8's 'No Step 2 of 4' and O11's instruction budget are stated as observations and owned by no check. Proposed: M9's grep gains an 'imperative second-person opener' clause with a named verb list, and O8 gains a numerals clause with its own method — a numeral drawn on any surface during creation that is not part of an authored sentence.

RI-CHR01's Distinctness 10 band ('540 signatures, >= 486 viable') and RI-CHR03's Decidability 0 band ('every sign viable with all 6') are satisfied by the same measurement. build-viability.mjs's first run on this build returns 540/540, which is simultaneously the best possible score on one and the worst possible on the other. One of the two bands is wrong and the corpus should decide which before either is used to move a build.

tools/harness/jrn09-exchange.mjs M3 cannot go red on NAMED_line while the writ draws the class name, because it tests `blob.indexOf(norm(c.class_name)) >= 0` over the whole walk instead of testing the naming line at its node. TOOL-LOOP rule 3 question 2 — 'can the tool fail?' — is unanswered for this check and the answer is no. A tool critic should run over the round-3 harness additions.

method_deviations.what: I did not run RI-CHR01's Legibility axis, RI-PRG02's M5 earned fraction, RI-PRG03's M7 skill-scales-damage and air-swings check, RI-EXP01 (whose five tools now exist), RI-PLT03 P1's T_control, or RI-JRN01's M1/M2/M3/M12/M14 through the newly-landed tools/journey/journey-run.mjs. All are scored unmeasurable => 0 per SCORING §1.1, and under min-over-axes that is what makes RI-CHR01, RI-PRG02 and RI-PRG03 report native 0. None of these is a corpus_debt any longer — every tool they need is on disk as of today — so each is a CRITIC debt and is recorded as mine rather than charged to the build.
method_deviations.why: The box was at load 37 on four cores with 42 chrome processes for most of this session and boot broke six times on another piece's half-written quest data. I spent the browser budget I had on the claims the dispatch asked me to disprove and on the one measurement nobody had ever taken (M4 clause 1), and I would make the same choice again. AGENT-PROTOCOL's new section says to say so rather than ship a number I could not take properly.

method_deviations.what: I wrote seven instruments during this critique: critic-w1-07-r3a.mjs (DTR against three denominators through the draw-call register), r3b (the (npc,race) census in bare Node), r3c (ES-NAMED with my own sweep shape and RNG, plus a floor sweep), r3d (M5 from a pixel readback, M20/HF9, M8), r3e (accessor coverage, with the third surface instrumented as a control), r3f (the strings the accessor cannot see), r3g (NAMED_line as the item defines it, beside the builder's test on the same runs). All are in the artifacts directory and all are declared here per TOOL-LOOP rule 1. None of them is a rename of a builder tool; none calls jrn09-exchange.mjs, chr-talk-probe.mjs or creation-audit.mjs for a headline number.
method_deviations.why: The builder wrote the instruments that grade RI-JRN09, and this project has been caught by that repeatedly. Two of the round's four headline claims survive my instruments unchanged (DTR_q = 1.0000 and NAMED_distinct = 14 of 14) and one does not (NAMED_line 100% -> 0%), which is the reason for the rule.

method_deviations.what: I did not attempt a blind pair for RI-JRN09 and recorded not_possible with a reason rather than leaving the field empty.
method_deviations.why: The item declares blind_pair: no and there is no captured Morrowind opening in the corpus to pair against.

method_deviations.what: RI-JRN01's native score is reported as raw/runnable over the 60 points I measured rather than as a fraction of 100, per §0.1(b)'s reporting rule, and the checks I did not run are listed explicitly rather than folded into the denominator.
method_deviations.why: The runnable weight moved this round when the A-JRN1 tools landed, and reporting a fraction of 100 would silently claim I had measured checks I had not.

arbitration_questions.question: RI-CHR01's Distinctness 10 band and RI-CHR03's Decidability 0 band are both satisfied by 540/540 viable signatures. Which band moves?
arbitration_questions.context: build-viability.mjs landed today and its first run makes the conflict concrete rather than theoretical. Distinctness is asking 'can you play any of these builds', Decidability is asking 'does the choice cost you anything', and a build that maximises the first necessarily zeroes the second as the two are currently written. Until this is resolved, RI-CHR03 cannot reach 6 without RI-CHR01 dropping below 10.

arbitration_questions.question: Does W1-07 own journey.firstlaunch.flow, and if not, who measures O6?
arbitration_questions.context: BAR-CRITIQUE-W1-07-R1 §R7 found that 45 of RI-JRN01's 100 points measure paths W1-07 does not declare, and that 37 of 38 journey.*/input.*/experience.* paths are owned by nobody.
